ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Using electrostatic dust removal can greatly reduce the dust in emitted flue gas. As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of an electrostatic dust removal device; flue gas enters from pipe opening M and is discharged from pipe opening N. When high voltage is connected to the two ends A and B, under the action of the electric field the air molecules in the pipe are ionized into electrons and positive ions, while after adsorbing electrons, the dust finally attaches to the metal pipe wall, thereby achieving the purpose of reducing dust in the emitted flue gas. According to the above principle, which of the following practices is correct? ( )
A. End A is connected to the high-voltage positive pole, and end B is connected to the high-voltage negative pole
B. End A is connected to the high-voltage negative pole, and end B is connected to the high-voltage positive pole
C. Both end A and end B are connected to the high-voltage positive pole
D. Both end A and end B are connected to the high-voltage negative pole

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Using electrostatic dust removal can greatly reduce the dust in emitted flue gas. As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of an electrostatic dust removal device; flue gas enters from pipe opening M and is discharged from pipe opening N. When high voltage is connected to the two ends A and B, under the action of the electric field the air molecules in the pipe are ionized into electrons and positive ions, while after adsorbing electrons, the dust finally attaches to the metal pipe wall. According to the above principle, what poles of the high voltage should end A and end B be connected to respectively?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Both end A and end B are connected to the high-voltage negative pole
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, flue gas enters from the lower-right pipe opening M, flows along the internal channel of the device, and then is discharged from the upper-left pipe opening N; many places in the figure are labeled “metal pipe wall,” indicating the pipe wall to which the dust finally attaches. Then reason: the stem states that air molecules are ionized under the action of the electric field to produce electrons and positive ions, and after the dust adsorbs electrons it becomes negatively charged and finally attaches to the metal pipe wall. To make the discharge electrodes in the pipe provide electrons and let the dust adsorb electrons, the electrodes connected to A and B should both serve as high-voltage negative electrodes. Therefore, both end A and end B should be connected to the high-voltage negative pole.
